Model: chemogenetic activation of hM3Dq+ Ach neurons (BF)
Effect: destabilized SWS

Model: chemogenetic activation of hM3Dq+ Glu neurons (BF)
Effect: destabilized sleep

Model: chemogenetic activation of hM3Dq+ GABA neurons (BF)
Effect: Increase wake (less REM and SWS)

Model: Activation of GABAergic (VGAT+) LH neurons innervating VLPO
Effect: Promotes wake for several hours, uninterupted 4-6 hrs
Other effects: prominent quantitative sleep rebound observed

Model: Conditional Knock-out Mice for vglut2
Effect: REM sleep decreased and fragmentation
Other effects: Glu+GABA in SLD contribute to REM atonia. Glu in cLDT and SLD important for REM gen.

Model: optogenetic activation of GABAergic neurons
Effect: 12-fold increase in REM sleep. Increased probability of transitions from NREM sleep to REM sleep. Prolonged REM sleep episodes when activated during REM sleep period.

Model: optogenetic activation of glutamatergic neurons
Effect: Induced wakefulness

Model: Optogenetic inhibition of GABAergic neurons
Effect: Caused 41% reduction of REM sleep duration

Model: Optogenetic activation of POA/RPA projecting galaninergic neurons
Effect: Supressed REM sleep and promoted NREM sleep.

Model: Optogenetic inhibition of POA/RPA projecting galaninergic neurons
Effect: Increased REM sleep and decreased NREM sleep.

Model: Optogenetic activation of RPA projecting galaninergic neurons
Effect: Increased REM sleep and decreased NREM sleep.

Model: Optogenetic inhibition of RPA projecting galaninergic neurons
Effect: Decreased REM sleep and increased NREM sleep.

Model: optogenetic activation of noradrenergic LC neurons
Effect: Inhibiting NREM to REM transition. Disruption of spindle formation during NREM sleep.
Other effects: Acumulation of REM sleep pressure

Model: Optogenetic inhibition of noradrenergic LC neurons
Effect: Enhanced density of sleep spindles. Reduced total time spent in NREM sleep and increasing time spent in REM sleep and wakefulness. Increases transitions from NREM to REM sleep.

Model: Kept awake for 4 hours by novelty introduction
Effect: Increased wakefulness and sleep pressure
Other effects: Some areas off, others on in a awake/sleep state

Model: Lesion of mPOA by NMDA
Effect: long-lasting insomnia with decrease in deep sleep and REM
Other effects: Reduce in bodyweight due to locomotion, less sleep pressure, hyperthermia

Model: Disk over water - forced locomotion
Effect: sleep deprivation, after 2-3 weeks dead unless halted
Other effects: TSD increase temp, excessive heat loss, attenuation of normal wake-sleep temp differences. Spotaneous death

Model: Bilateral lesion of VLPO using ibetonic acid
Effect: Decrease in NREM sleep time

Model: Dorsal lesion of VLPO using ibetonic acid
Effect: small change in NREM, loss of REM

Model: Lesion of VLPO using orexin-B-saporin
Effect: Rats with >70% cell loss slept up to 40% less than intact rats

Model: Inactivation of POA GABAergic neurons
Effect: Increased wakefulness and decreased sleep. Transitions from wake to sleep states were significantly reduced.

Model: Inhibition of POA CCK neurons
Effect: Increased wakefulness, reduced NREM and REM sleep

Model: Inhibition of POA Tac1 neurons
Effect: Increased wakefulness and decreased sleep.

Model: Activation of POA GAL neurons
Effect: Increased wakefulness and decreased sleep.

Model: forced confrontation with novelty
Effect: Increase activity, decrease in REM+NREM
Other effects: Sleep pressure rised after time, had to introduce more often. REM sleep affected after exposure

Model: forced confrontation with novelty
Effect: Increase activity, decrease in REM+NREM
Other effects: Sleep pressure rised after time, had to introduce more often. REM sleep affected after exposure

Model: Cage exchange
Effect: Increase activity, decrease in REM+NREM

Model: Cage exchange
Effect: Increase activity, decrease in REM+NREM

Model: forced confrontation with novelty
Effect: decrease NREM and REM, more pain
Other effects: Increase of both NREM and REM due to sleep pressure. Caffeine+modafinil blocked sleep-deprivation induced pain hypersensitivity

Model: Kept awake with aparatus + Activation of VTA DA neurons
Effect: Abolished NREM+REM. Sleep during critical period (P35-P42) shapes novelty preference
Other effects: Improving NREM sleep or reducing VTA activity during adolescent critical period can ameliorate social defecits

Model: Missense mutation of NALCN.
Effect: Shortened REM sleep episodes. Reduced REM sleep by 44%

Model: Knock-out Knac2 using homologous recombination
Effect: Pups had significantly less NREM sleep (~23%) and more waking (+21%). Higher number of waking episodes. Died at P28.
Other effects: KO pups between P12-P28 die due to generalized seizures

Model: Activation of the PB neurons
Effect: Reduce sleep by 50% the first day of CNO application, behavioural arousal
Other effects: subsequent PB activation produced progressively lesser wake amounts

Model: Activation of vglut2 neurons of the SuM region w/ CNO
Effect: Continuous wakefulness for ~12 hours after activation

Model: Activation of vgat/vglut2 neurons
Effect: Modest but significant effect on duration of wakefulness following CNO injection

Model: Activation of Nos1 positive neurons
Effect: Promoted wakefulness and increased sleep latency
Other effects: Inactivation led to reduced theta power during REM

Model: Activation of GABAergic neurons in medullary PZ
Effect: Increases SWS at expense of REM and Wakefulness
Other effects: deep SWS induced by CNO administration appeared to satisfy the homeostatic need for sleep

Model: Heterozygous clock mutation
Effect: Moderate reduction in sleep (-9%/1hr) due to decreased NREM sleep, mainly during DP.
Other effects: Less recovery sleep than WT, but more than homozygous.

Model: Homozygous clock mutation
Effect: Significantly less sleep (-18%/-2hrs) due to decreased NREM sleep. Shorter NREM episode length.
Other effects: Less recovery sleep and smaller increase in REM sleep.

Model: Hemideletion in chromosomal region 16p11.2 (risk for ASD)
Effect: Hyperactivity, male mice more awake and significantly less NREM sleep. Long bouts of consolidated wakefulness (>42 min)
Other effects: females had no difference to wt female mice. Males had increased alpha power during wake, while females had increased beta power during wake and decreased low delta power during NREM sleep.

Model: Lesion of hypothalamus with incision or hook
Effect: Displayed irregular sleep-wake cycle. Rats were unable to stay awake or sleep, went into a continous drowsy state.

Model: Lesion in BF+LC+TMN orexin neurons by different saporins
Effect: Reduced REM sleep by 44.4% (triple lesioned). Less and longer NREM+Wake bouts.
Other effects: Triple lesioned had additive effect on wake on NREM sleep (dark cycle)

Model: Lesion in BF+LC orexin neurons
Effect: Reduced REM sleep by 32.2% (double lesioned). Less and longer NREM+Wake bouts.

Model: Optogenetic activation of LC noradrenergic neurons
Effect: Immediate sleep-to-wake transitions. More wakefulness at expense of NREM sleep + reduced probability of sleep-to-wake transitions
Other effects: Decrease in SWA during NREM - decreased sleep depth. Decreased theta activity for REM. Affected locomotion. High frequent continuous stimulation resulted in behaviour arrest.

Model: Reduce REM sleep by flower pot method
Effect: REM sleep deprivation, ~45% decrease. NREM decrease if platform too high.
Other effects: also deprivation of deep NREM. Had increased REM sleep bout and total after flower pot.

Model: flower pot method
Effect: Reduces REM. SD rats was able to retain information less than 5 mins.
Other effects: also deprivation of deep NREM. Bad performance in maze tasks

Model: Sleep deprivation effect on different inbred mice strains
Effect: D2 and 129 most wakefulness. C easily held awake, stress sensitivity. AK + C needed longer sleep time, D2 needed least

Model: Acute exposure to corticoserone
Effect: acute rapidly increases wakefulness at expense of REM and NREM sleep
Other effects: Increase EEG delta during wake and decrease during NREM.

Model: Chronic exposure to corticoserone
Effect: Chronic led to excessive wakefulness and REM sleep, decrease NREM
Other effects: effects persisted, except for REM sleep amounts, even 7 days after the drug withdrawal. Decreased delta and increased theta during wake. theta power decreased during REM and delta power increased during NREM

Model: Cage exchange - male in a previously male occupied cage
Effect: Sleep disturbances hours after; prolonged sleep latency, reduced sleep duration, frequent arousals, fragmentation of sleep. Stress induced insomnia
Other effects: Lesions of the infralimbic cortex restoreNREM but not REM sleep in animals with experimental stressinduced insomnia. Lesions of the extended amygdala restored both REM and NREM sleep

Model: Modafinil-induced wakefulness
Effect: Promotes wake at expense of other sleep states, large dose = efficiently longer wake. Strongly induced Fos in TMN and orexin neurons of the PFx
Other effects: may promote waking via activation of TMN and orexin neuron

Model: Dose dependent use of caffeine
Effect: A dose-dependent and significant prolongation of sleep onset latency
Other effects: effect was sensitive to zolpidem and trazodone, both of which attenuated the caffeine-induced increase in SOL

Model: Dose dependent use of caffeine
Effect: 12.5+25mg/kg: Increased wakefulness, decreased total sleep time. 0.125+1.25mg/kg: increased SWS1 at expense of SWS2

Model: Diazepam IP injections in different doses (to treat sleep apnea)
Effect: 5mg/kg of diazepam increased NREM and decreased REM. Also reduced amount of wake and wake frequency.

Model: expose rodents to periods of hypoxia of 30-120s during light phase
Effect: Hypoxia cause REM sleep deficits and deficits in EEG delta power of NREM
Other effects: total NREM recovered over time, but not REM

Model: Expose rodents to auditory/tactile stimulus
Effect: Caused sleep fragmentation

Model: Using SeCl14 to block prostaglandin D synthase (PGDS) on WT
Effect: WT: increased wake, decreased NREM by 23% and REM by 44%. H-PGDS KO mice: increased wake, 80% reduced NREM+REM In L-PGDS KO mice, the effect on sleep and wake had delayed sleep onset during dark phase.
Other effects: treatment with this compound resulted in a distinct sleep rebound during the following dark period

Model: Using SeCl14 to block prostaglandin D synthase (PGDS) on L-PGDS KO mice.
Effect: 5mg/kg: In L-PGDS KO mice, the effect on sleep and wake had delayed sleep onset during dark phase.
Other effects: treatment with this compound resulted in a distinct sleep rebound during the following dark period

Model: Using SeCl14 to block prostaglandin D synthase (PGDS) on H-PGDS KO mice.
Effect: 5mg/kg: H-PGDS KO mice: increased wake, 80% reduced NREM+REM
Other effects: treatment with this compound resulted in a distinct sleep rebound during the following dark period

Model: DP1R antagonist ONO-4127Na infused into subrachnoid space(100pmol/min)
Effect: Reduced NREM by at max 23% and REM by max 50%, increased wakefulness
Other effects: treatment with this compound resulted in a distinct sleep rebound during the following dark period

Model: DP1R antagonist ONO-4127Na infused into subrachnoid space(200pmol/min)
Effect: Reduced NREM by at max 30% and REM by max 60, increased wakefulness

Model: Mice with iron deficiency (diet)
Effect: Increased wakefulness 4h period prior to lights-on. Both NREM+REM decreased, significant for NREM
Other effects: iron deficient less red blood cells

Model: Ntsr1 knockout mice
Effect: Reduced REM sleep in dark phase and increased amount of NREM sleep.
Other effects: Following sleep deprivation, NTSR1 knockouts exhibited more wake and less NREM rebound sleep

Model: Sleep patterns in different levels of anxiety in mice strains
Effect: High anxiety needed more sleep, due to heavy sleep fragmentation, lower quality of sleep. Had a drive for REM sleep.

Model: Platform method/flowerpot method with large and small diameter
Effect: REM virtually abolished during first light in both, NREM halved. Deeper NREM lower in small diameter group.
Other effects: REM rebound in both groups. Only NREM rebound in small diameter group.

Model: Homemade rotating device 'CaResS' for sleep fragmentation
Effect: REM significantly decreased (59-66%), SWS decreased (12-19%). Glucose absorption slower
Other effects: Increased GC level during active period

Model: Gentle handling
Effect: Almost total suppression of both NREM and REM sleep.
Other effects: less time awake in DP after automated depression in comparison to gentle handling. less in REM after deprivation than gentle handling

Model: Automated running wheel in cage, rotation triggered by EMG threshold
Effect: 99.5% suppression of both NREM and REM sleep.

Model: Automated rotating drum with fixed internal wall
Effect: 99% suppression of sleep, with REM completely abolished. Both LP and DP.

Model: Forced locomotion with treadmill for sleep fragmentation
Effect: NREM bout decreased and time decreased by 17%. REM absent.

Model: Forced locomotion with treadmill for sleep fragmentation for 6
Effect: REM and NREM significantly reduced.
Other effects: NREM duration and delta power increased after SI. Rats more sleepy after SI. BF AD increased after SI

Model: Forced locomotion with treadmill for sleep fragmentation for 24h
Effect: REM significantly reduced, NREM reduced. Last 18h of 24h NREM not reduced
Other effects: NREM duration and delta power increased after SI. Rats more sleepy after SI. BF AD increased after SI

Model: Forced locomotion with treadmill over water with motion det. IR camera
Effect: NREM sleep decreased about 50%. Near complete elimination of REM sleep.
Metabolic side effects: BW decrease, FI increased. Locomotion increased
Other effects: NREM not increased right after SD. REM sleep was elevated in all animals after SD.

Model: Orbital shaker for interupting sleep 30s every 2min for 48h
Effect: NREM decreased, bouts significantly reduced. REM sleep amount profoundly affected, but not bouts
Other effects: Rebound in REM sleep time and increase in depth of NREM delta power

Model: Activation of orexin neurons
Effect: Increased probability of awakening mice from sleep. Increased probability of awakening mice from sleep. High frequency stimulation reduced the latency from NREM and REM sleep to wakefulness. Chronic stimulation increased number of transitions from NREM to wakefulness.
Other effects: Effect diminished with sleep pressure induced by 2-4 hrs of sleep deprivation

Model: Activation of BF neurons using glutamatergic agonist (NMDA+AMPA)
Effect: Causes wakefulness
Reference: Cape, E. G. & Jones B. E. (2000)

Model: Inactivation of BF neurons using procaine
Effect: Loss of REM sleep
Reference: Cape, E. G. & Jones B. E. (2000)

Model: Lesion of accumbens core with ibotenic acid
Effect: Increase in wakefulness and reduction in NREM
Other effects: Excessive digging and scratching, OCD-like behaviour

Model: Lesion in GP using ibotenic acid
Effect: Substantial increase in wake (45.52%), frequent sleep-wake transitions, decrease in NREM
Other effects: Aphagia and adipsia, contributor to weight loss

Model: Blocking MCH1 receptor using MCH1 receptor antagonists
Effect: Compound A had dose-dependent decreases in deep NREM sleep and REM sleep and increases waking and passive waking states. Compound B significantly reduced deep NREM sleep and REM sleep, while increased wakefulness.
Other effects: No homeostatic rebound of sleep was observed, tendency for REM sleep recovery during dark phase

Model: Blocking mGlu2 receptors using agonist LY354740
Effect: Dose-dep. reduction in REM sleep, longer REM onset latency.

Model: Increase of glutamate effect using PAM BINA
Effect: Dose-dependent reduction in REM sleep. Slight enhancement in wake state.

Model: Using both LY354740 and BINA
Effect: Additive effects on supressing REM sleep and lengthened REM sleep onset

Model: MCH KO mice
Effect: More wakefulness (+90 min/24 hr) due to increased bouts. Reduced total NREM, sig. reduced REM sleep.
Other effects: Sleep rebound normal.  MCH KO mice profound inability to adapt to fasting. wake consolidation.

Model: MCH KO mice fasting
Effect: Hyperactivity, marked deficits in REM sleep. Some showing no REM sleep.
Other effects: Exagerated increase in locomotion.

Model: Loss of LAP protein MOP3
Effect: Loss of circadian rythm, no rythm to running periods. Not reactive to Light/Dark periods

Model: Restricted ibotenic acid lesions of the ventral or dorsal SPZ
Effect: Ventral: profound reduction of measures of circadian index of sleep. Loss of circadian rythm, esp during constant darkness
Other effects: dorsal lesions of SPZ disrupted circadian rythms in body temperature

Model: Perpetual avoidance of water on a wheel (PAWW)
Effect: Locomotor activity up during light phase, less daytime sleep. More nighttime sleepiness. fragmented sleep and reduced delta power
Other effects: body temp rythm was dysregulated during dark phase, plasma catecholamines elevated

Model: circadian disruption: 20 h long day, 10 h of light and 10 h of darkness
Effect: Disrupt sleep timing and quality of sleep (NREM delta power decrease)
Other effects: Innate immune response altered

Model: homozygous Tfap2b deletion in GABAergic neurons
Effect: Female: reduced sleep and NREMS delta power and REM theta power. Male: a decrease in the time spent in NREMS
Other effects: female:weaker delta and theta power during rebound sleep

Model: Heterozygous deletion of Tfap2b
Effect: Reduced sleep time and delta power during NREM. decrease in REM sleep duration and theta power. weaker SD response- Circadian rythm shortened
Other effects: Increased sleep pressure. Sleep loss phenotype stronger when knocked down during development vs.adult.

Model: Activation of PZ vglut2 neurons
Effect: Induced wakefulness due to increase in bout length, decrease delta frequency band power. NREM and REM decreased
Other effects: no sleep rebound seen
Reference: Erickson, E. T. M., et al. (2019)

Model: Activation of SLD vglut2 neurons
Effect: Induced wakefulness and enhanced REM sleep
Reference: Erickson, E. T. M., et al. (2019)

Model: Activation of PB vglut2 neurons
Effect: Induces wakefulness at expense of REM and NREM sleep.  No sleep rebound
Other effects: no sleep rebound seen
Reference: Erickson, E. T. M., et al. (2019)

Model: Activation of orexin neurons
Effect: When OX stimulated during both NREM and REM, mice had short-latency arousals. Higher frequencies were effective for NREM sleep transitions, while increased probability of REM sleep to wake transitions happened at lower frequencies.

Model: Response to novel stimuli after chemical LC lesion
Effect: Fell asleep unless new novelty every 1h. LC drives arousal and attention

Model: Novelty introduction
Effect: Increased wakefulness significantly when new novelty introduced every 1 hr

Model: Causing serotonin depletion using PCPA in mice and housing them in different temperatures
Effect: Mice couldn't regulate bodytemp - hypothermia. Hypothermic mice had increased wake at expense of NREM and REM sleep
Other effects: housing at 33°C, which is in the thermoneutral range for a mouse, prevented insomnia or any change in TC

Model: Activation of 5HT neurons
Effect: doubles amount of wake and reduces+fragments NREM sleep
Other effects: neuropathic pain accelerates the activity of DRN-5-HTergic neurons

Model: KO of DAT gene in mice and metamphetamine, modafinil and caffeine
Effect: Significantly increased wakefulness due to wake bout duration , while NREM sleep duration and bout length were reduced
Other effects: hyperactivity in novel environments. no response to amphetamine and modafinil. Hypersensitive to caffeine

Model: activation of the glutamatergic PPT neurons
Effect: Hm3 markedly increases wake for ~7 hours
Metabolic side effects: Less eating and exploring, run more on wheels

Model: activation of the GABAergic PPT neurons
Effect: Hm3 mildly reduce REM sleep and shortens latency to sleep onset

Model: Injection of orexin-A in WT, OX1R KO, OX2R KO and OX1R:OX2R KO mice
Effect: increases wake and suppresses REM for several hours. Activation of OX2R more than OX1R for wake, but OX1R for REM. No response for mice with KO of both receptors

Model: Activation of orexin neurons
Effect: awakens mice from REM and SWS sleep. Reduces latency, in a frequency-dependent matter, from NREM and REM sleep to wake.

Model: Activation of hM3Dq orexin neurons
Effect: increases wake and strongly suppresses REM sleep during light period

Model: Activation of GABAergic LH neurons innervating TRN
Effect: Activation during NREM sleep rapidly wakes mice from NREM sleep. Semi-chronic stimulation increased number of arousal transitions and total wakefulness.

Model: Silencing of GABAergic TRN projecting neurons
Effect: Silencing during NREM sleep rapidly wakes mice from NREM sleep.

Model: Lesion of GABA/glycinergic transmission into the PZ with saporin
Effect: Increase wakefulness (+50%) and wake bouts at expense of NREM (SWS) amount and bouts, insomnia

Model: Genetical disruption of PZ GABA neurons
Effect: Increase wakefulness (+40%) at expense of NREM and REM. Change in NREM due to sleep bouts, indicating deficit in sleep initiation

Model: Chemogenetic inhibition of PZ GABAergic neurons
Effect: Strongly decrease NREM (SWS)
Other effects: CNO-induced SWS at expense of both wake and REM

Model: Cortical neurons lacking nNOS
Effect: shorter NREM sleep bouts, less total NREM sleep, and a blunted homeostatic response to sleep deprivation
Other effects: greater delta power during wakefulness and decreased delta power during NREM sleep.

Model: ICV Injection with Orexin A
Effect: Increased arousal, significantly decreased REM
Other effects: dose-dependent decrease in plasma growth hormone levels. High dose (30µg) increase dopamine turnover

Model: ICV Injection with Orexin A
Effect: Dose-dependant increase in wake 2-3 hours after. Marked reduction in REM and deep SWS. REM latency prolonged

Model: ICV infusion of orexin-A
Effect: Substantial increase in wakefulness and significant decrease in both NREM and REM sleep.

Model: ICV infusion of [Ala11]orexin-B (agonist)
Effect: Dose-dependent increase in wakefulness and decrease in NREM and REM sleep. [Ala11]orexin-B was more potent than orexin-B.
Other effects: Sig. NREM decrease at 10 and 40 nmol of orex-b agonist. REM totally suppressed 2nd hour

Model: ICV infusion of orexin-B
Effect: Dose-dependent increase in wakefulness and decrease in NREM and REM sleep

Model: Injections of orexin-A/hcrt1 in LC
Effect: Suppressed REM sleep (dose-dep.), increased wakefulness at expense of deep SWS
Other effects: Injection of hcrt1 induced overexpression of c-fos in LC. hcrt2 (orex-b) not found in LC

Model: Striatial excitotoxic lesion
Effect: Increased wakefulness at 30 days post-lesion at expense of SWS duration. Increase in W bouts and SWS bouts duration.
Other effects: Sleep disturbances occur during light phase. Not strong significance in results

Model: Subcutanous injections of corticosterone (2mg in 0.01 ml oil)
Effect: initial enhancement of wakefulness and a reduction in slow-wave sleep within the first hour and lasted until hour 3
Other effects: Sig. increase in deep SWS and REM latencies.

Model: Repeated corticosterone injections
Effect: 7 days sign. decreased NREM sleep. 21 days shortened REM sleep latency.
Other effects: 7d: TH levels increased and GR expressopm decreased. 14+21d: enhanced REM, decreased TH+GR, FKBP51 expression increased

Model: Injections with PCPA and sleeping in different temperatures(20,30,32)
Effect: REM sleep and bout decreased after injection. SWS sleep and bout length decreased. W->SWS decreased. SWS->R increased
Other effects: bodytemp -2.3degrees after PCPA injection at 20 degrees.

Model: Acute cocaine through IP of three doses (3.6, 9.6, 18 mg/kg)
Effect: Dose-dep increased waking, especially first hour, and increase of EEG activity while awake. Increased sleep latency.
Other effects: Changes in waking time due to episode durtion, SWS and REM due to episode duration and number
Reference: Bjorness T. E. & Greene, R. W. (2018)

Model: Repeated cocaine use for 13 days
Effect: Increased waking, decreased SWS and REM during injection period. SWS and SWA dropped. Sleep latency and REM latency increased.
Metabolic side effects: Not measured, but low food intake
Other effects: Increase in gamma spectral energy, high EEG activity. Decrease in waking and increase in sleep during early and middle DP
Reference: Bjorness T. E. & Greene, R. W. (2022)

Model: Cocaine abstinence after chronic cocaine use
Effect: Increase in arousal for about 2 weeks. Increase in gamma energy Sleep latency increased.
Other effects: SWS SWE and W SWA remained elevated during early portion and increase in SWS during latter portion. Reduction in waking during early and middle DP
Reference: Bjorness T. E. & Greene, R. W. (2022)

Model: Heterozygous amino acid substitution at S246 to alanine in Hdac4
Effect: Decreased NREMS time, shorter NREMS episode duration and lower NREMS delta power
Other effects: NREMS delta power decreased at baseline and after sleep deprivation

Model: Heterozygous alanine substitution at Thr221 in Sik3 gene
Effect: Mildly decreased NREM sleep delta power, indicating impaired sleep depth

Model: Deletion of Sik3 in vglut2-positive neurons
Effect: Increase wake time, decreased NREM time and delta power at baseline and after SD.

Model: Deletion of Sik3 in vglut1-positive neurons
Effect: Increase wake time, decreased NREM time and delta power at baseline and after SD. milder than vglut2, but similar

Model: Deletion of Sik3 in vgat-positive neurons
Effect: Decrease in total REM sleep time

Model: Activation of dDpMe/vIPAG GABAergic neurons
Effect: Suppressed REM sleep and promoted NREM sleep. During wakefulness/NREM;prolonged NREMS and enhanced wake-to-NREM transitions
Other effects: Duration of wake after REM suppression decreased by 60.5% and NREM increased by 82.43%

Model: Inhibition of dDpMe/vIPAG GABAergic neurons
Effect: Induction of REM and decrease in NREM. Probability of NREM-REM 61.1%. REM sleep and wake durations were sig. increased after

Model: Global KO of Kcnn2 and Kcnn3
Effect: Kcnn2/3 KO sleep duration decreased (approx. -2,2h and approx. -1.85h). Awake state stabilization. Kcnn2 sig. decrease NREM
Other effects: Shorter sleep most of the day. Lower transition prob. from wake-sleep. Kcnn2 showed change in regulation of sleep

Model: Global KO of Camk2a and Camk2b
Effect: Significant decrease in sleep duration (approx- 0.9h and -2.0h resp).
Other effects: Camk2b KO less likely to transition from wake-sleep and sleep-wake.

Model: IP injection of PCP and MK-801 (NMDARs antagonists)
Effect: Decreased sleep duration. MK-801 sign. decrease of NREM sleep duration. Short-sleeper phenotype (SD?)

Model: Whole body deletion of Erk1
Effect: Significantly increased duration of wakefulness in both
Other effects: After SD, wakefuless was increased and NREM decreased

Model: neuro-specific deletion of Erk2
Effect: Significantly increased duration of wakefulness and significant decrease in  NREM sleep.
Other effects: After SD, wakefuless was increased and NREM decreased

Model: Inhibition of ERK phosphorylation
Effect: Increased wakefulness bout duration (mainly DP), +100min. Sig. decreased NREM, -100min. REM decreased. Sleep halved.
Other effects: After SD, NREM decreased by 1h. Phosphorylation reduced by 29.30% total, ERK2 by 37.85%. Delta power increased

Model: Selective activation (AL-OXB) of OXR2 in orexin KO mice by ICV
Effect: Increased wake time and bout duration. Reduced wake-NREM sleep transition frequency. Did not induce reward pathway in comparison to orexin-A.
Other effects: Ameloriate narcolepsy symptoms. Continious ICV injection make it last for 12h, decrease during dark phase. Didn't trigger reward pathways, less chance of addiction.

Model: Activation of orexin neurons using orexin-A in orexin KO mice
Effect: Increased wake time and wake bout duration 3h after injection, reduced wake-NREM transition frequency. REM also suppressed (not sig)
Other effects: Ameloriate narcolepsy symptoms. Continious ICV injection make it last for 12h, decrease during dark phase. Did trigger reward pathways - more chance of addiction

Model: Activation of PVH arginine vasopressin neurons (SSFO)
Effect: Immediate wakefulness from both NREM+REM, last 20-30min. Induced transitions to wake from NREM+REM.
Other effects: SSFO high specificity and efficency. Some leaked expression of SSFO to neighbouring nuclei

Model: Activation of PVH arginine vasopressin neurons
Effect: Increased time spent in wakefulness (+148,3%) and reduced NREM+REM (-45.9% and -59.2%)
Other effects: Sleep quality not changed after activation. Lasted for approx 7h. Activation ncreased number of c-fos-pos LHox

Model: Activation of PVH AVP projection neuronal fibers in LH
Effect: Induced awakefulness for ~25min. Rapidly induced transitions to wakefulness from both NREM+REM
Other effects: Orexin receptor antagonist suvorexant during activation drastically shortened duration of induced wake

Model: Administration of melanotan-II (melanocortin receptor agonist)
Effect: Significantly increased wakefulness and reduced NREM+REM(-44.7 and -86.1%). During 3h, wake increased +164.1%
Other effects: Sleep quality not altered after administration.

Model: Tfa2b+/- mice
Effect: Female show increased wakefulness and NREM sleep decreased, mainly during DP
Other effects: Decreased delta power during NREM sleep. Male exhibited a slight increase in EEG power during NREM.

Model: Generate Tfap2b mutant mouse strain
Effect: K114/K144 male reduced NREMS time (esp DP) and episode of wake was significantly increased

Model: Generate Tfap2b mutant mouse strain
Effect: K145/+ female episode number incr. and duration decr, of NREM during LP. Episode numbers of wake and REM also increased.

Model: Tfap2b deleted in nervous system during development
Effect: Increased wakefulness and decreased NREM sleep (episode number, esp LP). Circadian rytm deficits
Other effects: Increase in EEG power during wakefulness

Model: Tfap2b deleted postnatally by administrating tamoxifen
Effect: Decreased NREM sleep and increased wakefulness, esp during DP.
Other effects: Exhibit normal response to SD

Model: central 5-HT neuron ablation in mice using diphteria toxin + receptors
Effect: Decreased REM duration (-24.7%), fewer transitions from NREM-REM (-34.7%). Attenuated wake respnse to novel environment
Other effects: Increased theta power during wake. Decreased NREM sleep episode duration during DP.

Model: GLUT1 deficency syndrome mouse model using ENU i.p.
Effect: Longer wake times, shorter NREMS time.
Metabolic side effects: Reduced BW, glucose transport reduced, glucose metabolism increased, increased locomotion
Other effects: Homozygous are embryonic lethal. Decreased CBS fluid glucose value, convulsize seizures

Model: Loss of Gscl gene homologous recombinition using ES cells
Effect: Reduced REMS time and fewer REMS episodes. REM sleep latency increased. Slight increase in total NREM. Less NREM-REM transitions
Other effects: Also lacked expression of Dgcr14 in IP. Reduced theta power during REMS and increased arousability during REMS. Reduced REMS rebound

Model: Knock-out of MEf2D gene
Effect: Altered circadian rythm, with the sleep-cycle happened later during the day. . Fragmented sleep, sig. shorter REM latency. More transitions wake<->NREM.
Other effects: delayed activity onset (~25min) than WT and longer free-running period during dark(+40min). Also fragmented activity in comparison to WT. Clock gene expression normal.

Model: Overexpression of orexin in transgenic mice line
Effect: Fragmentation+reduced REM duration and latency.NREM decrease. Increase wake. incomplete REM sleep atonia

Model: Inhibiting LS GABAergic neurons (bipolar disorder mouse model)
Effect: Reduced sleep and heightened arousal.
Other effects: Increased irritable behaviour.

Model: Ablation of LS GABAergic neurons using casp3
Effect: Significant  increase in arousal and reduction in sleep. Sig. increase in wake and NREM episodes, while REM episodes decreased. Increase in NREM to wake and wake to NREM transition.
Other effects: Took longer to enter NREM after 6 hours of SD. Increased irritable behaviour.

Model: Activation of excitatory neurons in mPFC
Effect: Increased wakefulness duration.

Model: 6 hour sleep deprivation by introducing novel objects and cage change
Effect: Increased wakefulness. Increased gamma and theta frequency in EEG, delta reduced. Cortical activation.
Other effects: Increased sleep pressure and sleep rebound in subsequent recovery sleep (increased delta)

Model: Activation of astrocytes in the pons
Effect: Strongly suppressed REM sleeep due to increased episode numbers. Increased NREM sleep due to increased duration. Decreased transitions from wake to NREM, NREM to REM and REM to wake.
Other effects: Increased delta waves

Model: Activation of cortical neurons during NREM and REM sleep
Effect: Always woke mice up from NREM and REM sleep. REM needed more light stimulation.

Model: Activation of cortical neurons during NREM and REM sleep
Effect: Always woke mice up from NREM and REM sleep. REM needed more light stimulation. More effective in PtA (less light stimulation needed)
